first.description: Zendesk customer support and helpdesk platform; Ticketing API manages tickets, users, organizations, custom objects, and ticket workflows.

auth.summary: OAuth is recommended and required for multi-customer public integrations. OAuth access tokens use Bearer auth. Legacy API tokens use email/token Basic auth and are scheduled for permanent deactivation April 30, 2027. Password Basic auth is also documented but API password access must be enabled.

test_access.summary: Trial or existing Zendesk account; admins enable API access and accept developer/API terms. A sandbox is separately plan-gated; API credentials are not replicated there.

production_access.summary: Live API access requires an account, API activation, user permissions, and API operation entitlement. Public multi-customer distribution requires an approved global OAuth client; Zendesk Developer Terms prohibit sharing customer credentials.

interfaces.summary: JSON REST APIs; APIs span Ticketing, Help Center, Messaging/Conversations, Voice, Sales CRM, and other services. Ticketing reference links downloadable OpenAPI; Messaging publishes maintained YAML spec. No general Zendesk CLI confirmed in checked official docs.

mcp.summary: Zendesk Bridge provides vendor Zendesk MCP Server for data actions, currently open EAP by enrollment; over 400 tools, governed by agent identity and assigned permissions. Separate Zendesk MCP Client connects external MCP servers to Action Flows. Community reminia/zendesk-mcp-server is locally hosted. Composio has a Zendesk toolkit; catalog entry is a research lead, not proof of official server.

buildability.summary: Private build: wrap Ticketing REST with OAuth and account subdomain; test on trial/live account or eligible sandbox. Public build: obtain approved global OAuth client before customer rollout. Vendor MCP data integration is separately EAP-gated; Zendesk MCP Client is for developers integrating other MCP servers into Zendesk workflows.

first.blocker: For private API build, create account OAuth client and test on trial/account. For public route, request global OAuth client approval from Zendesk and obtain customer account consent. For vendor MCP route, enroll in External AI EAP and request server URL/tool catalog. Download Ticketing OAS via official reference link and parse locally to inventory operations.

verified.description: Zendesk Support API, also called Ticketing API; manages tickets, users, organizations, custom objects, and ticket workflows.

auth.summary: OAuth Bearer is supported. API tokens use Basic email/token auth and are deprecated. Password Basic is separately documented for end-user requests when enabled; public apps must use global OAuth.

test_access.summary: Test on trial or existing account after admin activates API access and accepts terms. Sandbox is a separate, plan-dependent option; tokens do not replicate into it.

production_access.summary: Live access requires an account, API activation, verified user, and operation-level role, permission, and plan entitlements. Public multi-customer distribution requires an approved global OAuth client; internal-use integrations are exempt.

interfaces.summary: Ticketing is JSON REST at `/api/v2`; reference includes a downloadable OpenAPI file and Postman collection. No general Ticketing SDK or CLI established from checked official docs.

mcp.summary: Zendesk Bridge is vendor MCP server in open EAP by enrollment; >400 tools, assigned by admins and governed by permissions. Zendesk MCP Client instead connects external MCP servers to Action Flows. Community server is maintainer-hosted; Composio toolkit is separate.

buildability.summary: Private build can wrap Ticketing REST with account OAuth and test on an account or eligible sandbox. Public build needs global OAuth approval. Bridge data access needs EAP enrollment; no vendor MCP implementation is assumed for the API route.

verified.blocker: Private API: create account OAuth client and use trial/account. Public API: request global OAuth approval, then use per-customer consent. Bridge: enroll in EAP and configure connection to obtain endpoint and assigned tools. Ticketing inventory: download official YAML and parse locally for operation count by family.

auth.summary: Private apps use workspace Access Tokens, issued to installing or last-regenerating teammate; public apps use OAuth. Both send Bearer authorization.

test_access.summary: Free US-only development workspaces support public-app development and OAuth testing; private-app testing may use existing paid workspace. Sandbox limits include 20 users/leads and disabled outbound email/push.

production_access.summary: Private live access requires an app on a paid workspace; no review. Public distribution requires OAuth, production app submission and Intercom review/approval; API plan restrictions may require active subscription.

interfaces.summary: HTTPS JSON REST; versioned API; SDKs and Canvas Kit. No vendor GraphQL or API CLI documented in checked developer references.

mcp.summary: Intercom-hosted remote MCP at https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp; 13 tools; US-hosted workspaces only. Streamable HTTP recommended; legacy SSE deprecated. OAuth or bearer token. Community MCP not established by checked sources.

buildability.summary: REST wrapper, vendor MCP reuse, and free US sandbox-first route documented. Live private route needs paid workspace/app access; public route needs OAuth configuration and review.

first.blocker: For private route, obtain paid workspace admin access and create app/token. For public route, obtain US development workspace, configure OAuth/scopes and HTTPS callback, build production app, provide installation URLs, submit for review. Confirm required paid plan for each intended endpoint against its operation docs/workspace.

verified.description: Support and Helpdesk platform. Intercom and Fin Developer Platform exposes REST APIs, SDKs, Canvas Kit and hosted MCP.

auth.summary: Private app Access Tokens serve the app’s own workspace; public apps use OAuth for customer workspaces. Both use Bearer authorization for REST.

test_access.summary: Public-app development uses a free US development workspace. It is limited to 20 users/leads; outbound email and push are unavailable. Private-app testing can use a paid workspace.

production_access.summary: Private apps run on the developer’s paid workspace without review. Public apps require OAuth and Intercom review before distribution. API access can have operation-specific plan restrictions.

interfaces.summary: Versioned HTTPS JSON REST API; SDKs and Canvas Kit. No official API CLI established in checked SDK documentation.

mcp.summary: Vendor-hosted remote MCP has US and EU endpoints; AU unsupported. Current guide documents 16 tools, OAuth or Bearer authentication, and region-specific endpoints. Earlier 13-tool/US-only description is stale. Community-maintained MCP status remains unresolved.

buildability.summary: REST wrapper or vendor MCP reuse is documented. Public development can start in a free US workspace; private live use requires paid workspace access, and public distribution requires review.

verified.blocker: Private route: obtain paid workspace teammate/admin access, create app and Access Token. Public route: obtain US development workspace, set OAuth scopes and HTTPS callback, prepare production app and installation URLs, then submit for review. Confirm plan and workspace-feature gates for each target operation in its current reference.

first.description: Freshworks cloud helpdesk for ticketing, customer contacts and companies, conversations, agents, groups, and knowledge-base content. Current publisher variants: Freshdesk Standalone 2021 and Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026; selected variant must be confirmed in the customer account.

auth.summary: API v2 documents user API key over HTTP Basic: username=API key, password=any dummy value; Base64(APIkey:X) as Authorization when setting header manually. User key belongs to an agent and inherits that role. Service-account keys are supported separately; service accounts have role, ticket-scope and group controls. Legacy username/password also mentioned by support. OAuth scopes are listed per operation, but Freshdesk API OAuth grant and endpoints were not found in checked API reference; OAuth is not supported by the official MCP endpoint. No secondary secret is needed for Basic API-key auth; rotation’s secondary key is an alternate API credential, not a companion secret.

test_access.summary: New account has a 14-day trial with feature access; API trial limit is documented as 50 calls/minute. Freshdesk configuration sandbox is a separate admin-enabled feature limited to Enterprise in current plans; it copies settings, not customer tickets/contacts, and has sample data. The sandbox is not required for direct API development.

production_access.summary: Live API uses tenant’s HTTPS Freshdesk domain and the same role-bound API key. Current Free API limit is 0; Growth is first documented paid API-enabled tier at 100 calls/minute (endpoint sublimits apply). Freshdesk Free Program may be available for six months, but its API access is not established by current sources; verify in tenant before relying on it.

interfaces.summary: Public REST API v2, JSON over HTTPS. Freshworks App SDK and FDK CLI support Freshdesk app development. API resource URLs use tenant domain plus /api/v2/resource. No GraphQL or gRPC interface documented in checked reference.

mcp.summary: Official Freshworks data MCP is generally available from 2026-09-10 on Freshdesk Standalone 2021 and Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026. Remote HTTP endpoint https://<subdomain>.freshdesk.com/mcp; API-key header. Actions operate on live customer data. No official developer-task MCP for Freshdesk API/app-building found. Community Freshdesk MCP source exists, but public evidence reviewed did not establish maintainer details/auth coverage. Composio lists a Freshdesk toolkit (182 tools; API-key authentication), a lead rather than proof of vendor MCP.

buildability.summary: Direct v2 wrapper is a currently justified production route on API-enabled Growth/Pro/Enterprise, subject to tenant key/role and rate limits. Official MCP reuse is justified for supported product variants and Growth or above. FDK is a separate route for Freshworks platform apps; app install/distribution requires product account and account-admin capability.

first.blocker: For wrapper: obtain tenant's exact Freshdesk variant/domain, Growth-or-higher subscription (or confirmed API-enabled trial), verified user key or approved service-account key, and role permissions for selected operations. For MCP: confirm supported product variant and Growth+ plan, retrieve endpoint/key, confirm MCP enabled and client network/IP allowlisting. For public app: create developer account, active Freshworks product subscription, package with FDK and submit for reviews.

verified.description: Freshworks cloud customer-support platform for tickets, contacts, companies, conversations, agents, and knowledge-base resources.

auth.summary: API v2 supports an agent API key as HTTP Basic username with dummy password `X`; no companion secret. Key inherits agent role. A service-account key is a separate non-human credential with role, ticket-scope, and group restrictions; primary/secondary keys support rotation. Reference scopes annotate operations but do not establish an OAuth flow. Official MCP supports API-key auth only.

test_access.summary: New accounts receive a 14-day trial; API limit is 50 calls/minute. Enterprise sandbox is an admin-provisioned configuration test environment with sample data, not a copy of live customer tickets or contacts.

production_access.summary: Live API: Growth, Pro, and Enterprise have 100, 400, and 700 calls/minute respectively; Free is 0. Trial’s 50/minute is temporary. Account-specific API limit rollout and endpoint sublimits may apply. Official MCP requires Growth, Pro, or Enterprise and supported editions; Free excludes MCP actions.

interfaces.summary: REST API v2, JSON over HTTPS, tenant-domain base URL. Official Freshworks CLI/FDK targets Freshworks apps; it is not a standalone Freshdesk API SDK. No GraphQL or gRPC interface established in checked reference.

mcp.summary: Freshworks hosted data MCP is generally available for Freshdesk Standalone 2021 and Freshdesk Unified Omni 2026. Remote endpoint is tenant `/mcp`, using the API key in Authorization header; calls operate on tenant data. Community implementations exist: effytech/freshdesk_mcp documents ticket tools and Freshdesk API integration; its maintainer identity/auth coverage were not established from repository pages checked. Composio catalog is a third-party toolkit lead, not vendor MCP evidence.

buildability.summary: Justified routes: REST wrapper on an API-enabled tenant; official MCP reuse on supported Growth-or-higher edition; both require tenant credentials and role access. Freshworks app development is a separate FDK route with developer and product-account prerequisites.

verified.blocker: Confirm tenant’s exact Freshdesk edition, domain, plan, account API limit rollout, and region. Obtain a verified agent key or approved service-account key with operation permissions. For MCP, confirm supported edition, plan entitlement, admin enablement, and network allowlisting. For public apps, obtain developer account, complete publisher submission, and approval.

first.description: Front customer communication and support platform. Core API manages company resources; conversation MCP connects external AI clients as teammates. Category: Support and Helpdesk.

auth.summary: Core API accepts OAuth 2.0 access tokens or Front API tokens; both use Bearer authorization. API tokens are created by company admins and apply at company level. Public partner integrations must use OAuth unless Front grants an exception. MCP authorization is distinct: it uses user-scoped authorization, allowing any teammate to connect.

test_access.summary: Free developer account provides a non-production environment, capped at 3 teammates. Existing production Front accounts can also be used for testing; developer account is recommended to avoid production data. Company admin required to create/manage API tokens and apps.

production_access.summary: Live production use requires an active Front customer instance; Front lists Starter, Professional, Enterprise paid plans. Private apps are available inside their creating instance. Public App Store launch requires partner submission, technical review/approval, OAuth, and ongoing support; no listing fee. No temporary live trial for production API use documented.

interfaces.summary: Core API is JSON REST. Platform also has Plugin SDK, Channel API, webhooks, Front MCP and Admin MCP. Core API has no official general-purpose SDK confirmed; official Plugin SDK is NPM package @frontapp/plugin-sdk.

mcp.summary: Official vendor conversation MCP: mcp.frontapp.com/mcp; OAuth/user-scoped, available to compatible clients and official assistant directories. Reads/searches conversations and contacts; can draft/send replies, post internal comments, tag, assign and change status. Admin MCP is separate open beta at mcp.frontapp.com/admin-mcp for configuration, admin-only; cannot delete resources. No community-maintained integration claimed. Composio Front toolkit is a research lead, not evidence of an API/MCP absence; catalog lists 180 tools, version 20261101_00, managed OAuth unavailable.

buildability.summary: Justified routes: wrap Core REST API; reuse official conversation MCP; develop first in free developer sandbox. Need a Front developer/customer account and company-admin role for tokens/apps. Public route additionally needs OAuth and Front technical approval.

first.blocker: For private build, create a free developer account and company-admin API token. For public distribution, create developer-account app, configure OAuth, build/test, then submit Front’s partner form for technical review. For a count tied to immutable schema, retrieve the GitHub commit SHA for core-api/core-api.json and count HTTP methods under paths.

verified.description: Front is a hosted customer communication and support platform. Core API and vendor MCP expose support data and actions. Category: Support and Helpdesk.

auth.summary: Core API accepts API tokens or OAuth access tokens as Bearer credentials. Company admins issue API tokens; public partner integrations require OAuth unless Front grants an exception. OAuth Client ID/Secret identify and authenticate the app at token exchange. MCP uses separate OAuth 2.1 + PKCE and user-scoped tokens. App Channel UID/secret are separate credentials.

test_access.summary: Free developer environment has no production data and a 3-teammate cap. Separate Front customer trial is 14 days on Professional with stated usage limits. Existing production account may be used for testing. Company admin needed for API tokens and apps.

production_access.summary: Live Core API access is available on customer plans; current listed plans are Starter, Professional, Enterprise, and the website offers a 14-day trial. Starter is the lowest listed paid tier. Private apps are confined to their Front instance. Public App Store route requires OAuth, submission, technical approval, and ongoing support.

interfaces.summary: Core API is JSON REST; Front also documents Channel API, webhooks, Plugin SDK, Connectors, and vendor conversation/Admin MCP. Official SDK found: @frontapp/plugin-sdk; no general Core API SDK or CLI established.

mcp.summary: Official vendor conversation MCP at https://mcp.frontapp.com/mcp is available across plans; it serves teammate-scoped conversation data/actions. Admin MCP at https://mcp.frontapp.com/admin-mcp is separate, open beta, admin-only, and has no delete tools. Current developer docs specify OAuth 2.1 + PKCE, confidential client credentials, no DCR, and read/write/send scopes. No community-maintained Front MCP integration was verified. Composio FRONT catalog is a research lead, not evidence of vendor MCP absence.

buildability.summary: Justified routes: Core REST wrapper, vendor MCP client, or sandbox-first development. Obtain Front developer/customer account; company admin needed for Core API token/app setup. Public distribution additionally needs OAuth and Front technical approval.

For exact operation counts, pin GitHub commit SHA for core-api/core-api.json and enumerate methods under paths by resource family.

production_access.summary: Live API calls use the hosted tenant’s region and token. Minimum plan and trial availability not specified in checked public API documentation; obtain tenant access and Admin-created token.

verified.description: Hosted B2B support platform; API exposes customer and issue data.

test_access.summary: A Pylon tenant and Admin-created token are documented prerequisites. Separate sandbox availability remains unverified.

production_access.summary: Hosted API access requires a tenant token and matching US or EU region. Minimum plan and trial eligibility are unresolved.

interfaces.summary: REST API; official TypeScript, Python and Go SDKs; experimental CLI. Issues reference embeds OpenAPI 3.0.3, info version 1.0.0.

mcp.summary: Composio lists a hosted PYLON_MCP toolkit with 12 tools. Pylon documentation MCP is for querying docs; no first-party customer-data MCP was established.

mcp.summary: First-party tenant MCP server at `/api/mcp`, Streamable HTTP. Personal MCP provides role-permitted tools; AI-agent MCP has selected tools and ticket/knowledge-base restrictions. Community MCP not confirmed in checked sources.

production_access.summary: Production API access starts at Standard. Standard excludes reporting endpoints; Plus and Pro include them.

interfaces.summary: HTTPS REST APIs: Inbox v2, with selected v3 routes, and Docs v1. Official PHP client; community SDKs and hscli CLI are also listed.

mcp.summary: Vendor-hosted remote MCP at https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp; new connections are read-only and authorize as each user. buildability.summary: Private API wrapper and first-party hosted MCP routes are documented, each requiring a tenant user’s authorization. Public app route requires Developer Portal registration, Sandbox conversion, OAuth, and approval.

first.product: Gladly Team (customer service platform; formerly Gladly Hero)

test_access.summary: API access requires a Gladly account, an administrator-assigned API User permission, and an API token. A sandbox is optional and may need to be purchased or included in the implementation package.

production_access.summary: Production API access requires an organization instance and API User permission/token. No public self-serve free tier or API trial is documented. Exact minimum commercial plan is not published in reviewed sources.

No Gladly REST MCP endpoint for general customer-data access established. Community server not confirmed; Composio catalog discovery supplied Gladia speech toolkit results, not Gladly.

buildability.summary: Build private customer-data integration by wrapping REST API after obtaining an API User/token; test in purchased/assigned sandbox when available. Public route exists for public Answers without token, with CORS enablement requiring Gladly Support for browser calls.

first.product: Slack Platform (Slack Web API and Slack apps)
first.description: Slack is a communications platform. Its Web API lets authorized apps query and change workspace data; Slack apps can also receive events and use other platform APIs. This brief treats “Slack” as the vendor platform rather than a customer-specific Slack edition.

auth.summary: Slack apps use OAuth 2.0, with bot tokens acting as the app and user tokens acting for the authorizing user. App client ID and client secret identify the OAuth client; the client secret is not the API bearer token. Other token classes include app-level, configuration, test, and legacy tokens; Slack’s documentation does not make every token class interchangeable. General app tokens do not expire unless revoked; optional token rotation supplies expiring access and refresh tokens.

test_access.summary: Slack Developer Program membership is free. Members can provision a full-featured Enterprise organization sandbox; provisioning requires a paid plan or valid payment method for identity verification, and an enterprise org admin may require approval. This sandbox is for development/testing and does not grant live-customer access.

production_access.summary: Production access is per workspace or organization: an app must be installed and granted its requested scopes; admins may review or approve installation. An undistributed app is confined to its associated workspace. Unlisted distribution supports pilots, while commercial distribution at scale should use Marketplace listing and review. No generic API free tier or production trial is documented by the sources checked.

interfaces.summary: Slack Web API is HTTPS HTTP RPC, with method-family.method paths. The platform also documents Events API and Socket Mode, SDKs and Slack CLI. It explicitly describes Web API as not REST.

mcp.summary: Slack provides the vendor-hosted remote MCP server at https://mcp.slack.com/mcp for agents accessing workspace data, plus vendor developer skills/plugin resources for building Slack apps. MCP use requires OAuth and may require workspace-admin approval. These are distinct from Slackbot acting as an MCP client to a developer’s server.

buildability.summary: A private integration can wrap Slack Web API or reuse vendor MCP after a workspace install/OAuth grant. Start in a Developer Program sandbox. Live customer execution still needs customer workspace authorization and scopes; commercial public distribution adds Marketplace review requirements.

first.blocker: For development, join Developer Program and provision sandbox (paid plan or payment method; org approval may apply), create app, and implement OAuth for minimum scopes. For customer pilot, enable unlisted distribution and obtain a customer workspace install/grant. For commercial scale, meet Marketplace prerequisites and submit for review.

verified.product: Slack Platform: Slack apps and Web API
verified.description: Slack-hosted communications platform. Slack apps use APIs to read and change workspace data; app functions, events, and developer tools are separate interfaces.

auth.summary: Slack apps use OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow. Bot tokens act as the app; user tokens act for the authorizing user. Client ID identifies the app; client secret authenticates it in OAuth exchanges. App-level, configuration, test, and legacy tokens are distinct token classes, not generic substitutes. Bearer tokens do not expire unless revoked, except when rotation is enabled.

test_access.summary: Developer Program membership is free. Enrolled developers may provision a basic sandbox; paid plan or valid payment method unlocks additional features. Enterprise organization admin can require sandbox approval. Sandboxes are for development/testing, not customer workspaces.

production_access.summary: Live data access requires installation and granted scopes in each workspace; administrators can screen and selectively approve installs. Unlisted distribution supports pilots. Commercial distribution requires Marketplace review. No universal Slack API plan minimum established; app category and specific APIs may impose gates.

interfaces.summary: Web API uses HTTPS HTTP-RPC methods, not REST. Slack also documents Events API, Socket Mode, SDKs, Bolt frameworks, and Slack CLI.

mcp.summary: Slack-hosted MCP server is at https://mcp.slack.com/mcp. It gives agent clients workspace data/actions; OAuth and approved app status are required. Slack Skills Plugin supports developer tasks. Slackbot is a separate MCP client that calls external servers. No community server maintainer verified.

buildability.summary: Build private integrations via Web API or vendor MCP. Sandbox supports development; live use needs workspace installation, scopes, and any admin approval. Public Slack Marketplace route requires review and install/usage thresholds.

verified.blocker: For API development, provision sandbox and create app with minimum scopes. For MCP, use internal app or complete Marketplace publishing, configure client ID/redirect URI, then obtain workspace approval and OAuth. For commercial listing, reach 10 active workspaces, satisfy current usage criterion, submit functional app and demo, and pass review.

first.description: Twilio communications platform APIs for messaging, voice, phone numbers, and related services.

auth.summary: REST API: preferred API Key SID + secret via HTTP Basic; include Account SID to select account. Main/Standard/Restricted keys differ in resource access. Legacy Account SID + Auth Token also uses Basic; Auth Token is fallback/operation-specific. OAuth 2.0 supports Client Credentials and Authorization Code, with Bearer access tokens. Test Account SID + Test Auth Token only for supported simulations.

test_access.summary: Self-serve 30-day trial with product-specific units and restrictions. Legacy test credentials remain usable if previously created; new Console cannot create them. Test credentials only cover listed legacy resources and magic inputs; requests elsewhere return 403.

production_access.summary: Production use requires an upgraded, funded account for full functionality; usage is metered. Upgrade removes trial restrictions and grants post-upgrade free units. Product, destination, sender, regional, and compliance gates remain route-specific.

interfaces.summary: HTTPS REST APIs, server-side helper SDKs, Twilio CLI, webhook callbacks, TwiML and client-side SDKs. No GraphQL or gRPC found in checked first-party API overview.

mcp.summary: Official Twilio MCP Public Beta at https://mcp.twilio.com/docs; Streamable HTTP, no authentication. Search and retrieve Twilio documentation/API operation schemas only; it does not execute customer-data actions. Public Beta terms: unsupported by Twilio support/SLA. Older Twilio Labs MCP availability article says experimental; current official twilio/ai repository README supersedes it. Composio lists a Twilio toolkit (452 tools, 45 triggers per catalog page), a third-party execution route. Discovery supplied no direct Twilio MCP Composio match.

buildability.summary: Public docs/API MCP routes can be built now. REST client can be developed with test credentials for limited simulated operations. Any live customer-data or communication route needs Twilio account credentials, configured sender/product, and applicable billing/compliance gates.

first.blocker: For private API integration, obtain a customer-provided Account SID, region, and least-privilege API key SID/secret (or OAuth credentials where supported), plus sender/service SIDs and product/compliance approvals. For public user-consented OAuth distribution, obtain organization OAuth app approval/configuration, redirect URI, client ID/secret and explicit permissions. Pin exact twilio-oai commit and compute operation inventory from the spec paths/methods before generating production code.

verified.description: Twilio public-cloud communications platform; scope here: Programmable Messaging, Voice, Phone Numbers, and IAM APIs.

auth.summary: API Key SID:secret uses HTTP Basic; Account SID selects account and is not the key. Account SID:Auth Token is a separate Basic credential for documented routes. OAuth uses client credentials at token exchange and Bearer access tokens for API calls. Client SDK Access Tokens are separate credentials.

test_access.summary: Self-serve trial lasts 30 days, with product-unit, geography, recipient, and content limits. Legacy test credentials work only for documented endpoints and do not change account state or contact real numbers; new Console cannot create them.

production_access.summary: Trial permits limited live use. Upgrade and fund the account for full functionality; eligible post-upgrade units are free before metered billing. Product, sender, destination, regional, and compliance gates can still apply.

interfaces.summary: HTTPS REST APIs, official server-side helper SDKs, Twilio CLI, webhooks/TwiML, and client SDKs. The checked first-party overview documents REST; GraphQL/gRPC are outside this brief.

mcp.summary: Official Twilio docs/spec MCP is Public Beta, unauthenticated, Streamable HTTP, and for developer research only. Older Twilio Labs MCP was described as alpha/unsupported. Composio lists a third-party Twilio toolkit; that catalog is a research lead, not evidence of a vendor MCP server.

buildability.summary: Docs/spec MCP and REST client development are available now. Limited simulation requires legacy test credentials. Live customer actions require account credentials, selected region, enabled product and sender configuration, plus applicable funding and compliance.

verified.blocker: For private live route, obtain customer Account SID, region, Restricted API Key SID/secret with needed operation permissions, sender/service IDs, and product/compliance access. For public user-consent route, configure Organization OAuth app, redirect URI, client ID/secret, and permissions. Pin immutable twilio-oai commit and count path/method operations before generation.

test_access.summary: Free edition supports developer-platform components; My Extensions contain sandbox versions for testing. Not a separate API sandbox tenant.

production_access.summary: Public API is usable on Free; API/component quotas vary by plan. Private extension sharing uses a published installation link; Marketplace distribution requires registered Zoho Marketplace Partner account and review.

buildability.summary: Public/private REST integration is buildable with OAuth and Cliq account; vendor MCP can be reused for client workflows. Cliq extensions have sandbox versions for development before publish.

first.product: Lark Open Platform — Lark’s overseas developer platform; custom (enterprise) and store (ISV) apps. Edition resolved from publisher API docs. Public research only; no customer actions.

test_access.summary: Developer Console app and test-company flow provide review-free API testing. Requires a Lark developer account and app ownership/collaborator role; up to 3 test companies per developer, 100 users each. These limits are sandbox limits, not production quotas.

production_access.summary: Production API access requires an official app version and tenant installation/approval. interfaces.summary: RESTful OpenAPI over HTTPS/JSON; official Node, Python, Go, Java SDKs and Lark CLI. Lark also publishes local OpenAPI MCP. No inspected immutable machine-readable API specification was found; operation count is unknown.

buildability.summary: API wrapper and reuse of official local MCP are currently justified. Sandbox-first is available, but live operation is also documented. interfaces.summary: REST over HTTPS/JSON. Official Node, Python, Go and Java SDKs and Lark CLI. No immutable complete machine-readable spec verified; full operation count unknown.

production_access.summary: Public API addon is available on all Pumble plans; Free plan supports the API route. MCP also has no paid-plan gate documented.

mcp.summary: Pumble-operated hosted MCP provides workspace content and actions; scopes determine available tools. No separate community server is established by checked sources.

test_access.summary: Requires a Pumble workspace to install the API addon or create an MCP app. No separate API sandbox or test credentials documented.

production_access.summary: API addon is documented as available on all plans, including Free. MCP minimum plan and public integration distribution gates remain unspecified.

interfaces.summary: HTTP API with linked Swagger reference; hosted MCP uses HTTP transport. API version and complete base URL remain unverified.

mcp.summary: Pumble hosts an MCP server for workspace data and actions. Tool exposure depends on selected app scopes. No community server was verified from the sources checked.

buildability.summary: Private integrations can use the API or hosted MCP after workspace setup and credential issuance. Pumble says public integrations are possible, but public listing and review steps are unresolved.

test_access.summary: Create a developer app and test it on a user account or a server not actively used by others. Discord describes creating a test server as free; no separate API sandbox or trial established.

production_access.summary: Public bot/app routes are available after app creation and installation; no paid API plan documented. verified.description: Discord app platform for HTTP API v10, WebSocket Gateway, and interactions.

test_access.summary: Create app and test on own account or isolated server. Docs describe no separate API sandbox.

production_access.summary: No paid API plan documented. Ordinary app installs are available; privileged intents require approval before verification. Discovery and monetization have separate eligibility gates.

buildability.summary: A direct wrapper can target the official cloud API after obtaining a bot token. Optional self-hosted server is a separate operator-managed route.

first.product: WhatsApp Business Platform — Cloud API; Meta-hosted Graph API v27.0 reference. On-Premises API retired 2025-10-23.

auth.summary: Bearer access tokens. User tokens can come from OAuth; server integrations commonly use system-user or Business Integration System User tokens. No API key or client secret is sent as the Graph API credential.

verified.description: Productivity and Project Management; Notion public-cloud API, OAuth connections, and hosted MCP.

test_access.summary: No separate API sandbox documented. Use a development workspace and PAT or internal connection; PAT creation and internal-connection creation depend on workspace policy/owner rights. Share pages with internal connections.

production_access.summary: REST API has no paid-plan requirement established in reviewed docs; Free plan permits API use subject to credential policy. interfaces.summary: HTTPS JSON REST API, official JavaScript/TypeScript SDK, official `ntn` CLI, and hosted Streamable HTTP MCP. No GraphQL or gRPC identified in checked publisher references.

mcp.summary: Official hosted Notion MCP is actively maintained at `https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`; OAuth client auth and optional Business/Enterprise MCP tokens. auth.summary: PAT and OAuth bearer tokens. Legacy API keys stopped working February 1, 2024.

test_access.summary: No dedicated sandbox established. Developer can use an Airtable account and authorized base; OAuth app testing uses the OAuth reference and example setup repository.

production_access.summary: Public API is available on all plans with plan call limits. Enterprise-only scopes/features and organization policy gates apply; admins can block MCP or require allowlisting.

interfaces.summary: REST/JSON Web API; MCP hosted service uses Model Context Protocol. OAuth uses HTTP endpoints.

mcp.summary: Official Airtable-hosted MCP supports data and developer tasks; community servers also exist. MCP client is required. Official endpoint uses OAuth or PAT; access follows Airtable permissions and org controls.

buildability.summary: Public route can wrap REST API with an account, authorized base, and PAT or OAuth. Private/customer-data route can reuse official hosted MCP after client auth and organization approval.

auth.summary: PAT and OAuth bearer access tokens. Legacy API keys no longer work. OAuth client secret is optional and used for server-side token requests; PAT and OAuth tokens represent a user or, for supported Enterprise Scale use, a service account.

test_access.summary: No isolated Web API sandbox documented. Test with an Airtable account and authorized base; OAuth example repository supports integration testing.

production_access.summary: Public API and hosted MCP are available across plans; Free and Team monthly API caps apply. Enterprise Scale admins can restrict third-party integrations; OAuth integrations need support email, privacy policy, and terms URL before authorization outside development.

interfaces.summary: REST/JSON Web API, OAuth over HTTP, hosted remote MCP over HTTP, official JavaScript client, and official MCP CLI.

mcp.summary: Official hosted MCP supports data work and base-building tasks; compatible MCP client required. Independent community servers exist, including Rashid Azarang's project. Hosted endpoint is vendor-run; client is not the server.

buildability.summary: REST route can run against an authorized production base with PAT/OAuth. Hosted MCP can be reused when the user has permitted bases and organization policy allows the integration.

verified.blocker: For REST, create least-privilege PAT or OAuth integration and test against an authorized base. For MCP, connect a compatible client and ask organization admin to allowlist if blocked. For public OAuth use, fill required support email, privacy policy and terms URLs, then verify distribution options in Builder Hub.

test_access.summary: Use a Linear workspace for development; docs recommend a separate workspace to manage OAuth apps. No public API sandbox or trial API environment documented.

production_access.summary: API and MCP are included on Free; Free limits workspace to 250 issues and 2 teams. OAuth app setup requires admin access to Settings > Administration > API. Paid workspaces may require app install approval.

first.description: Atlassian’s cloud project and work tracking product. Current product name is Jira; Jira Software and Jira Work Management were combined under Jira in 2024.

auth.summary: For integrations, Atlassian recommends OAuth 2.0 authorization-code 3LO. Personal API tokens use Basic auth for scripts; scoped tokens use the Atlassian API gateway. MCP also supports service-account API keys with Bearer auth, if an organization admin enables token authentication.

test_access.summary: A free Jira Cloud site can exercise REST API calls; Free supports up to 10 Jira users. An existing Atlassian account and a site are needed. No dedicated REST API sandbox documented in sources checked.

production_access.summary: REST API routes are documented for Jira Cloud. Jira Free supports up to 10 users; Standard, Premium and Enterprise are separate plans. Endpoint access still requires valid user permissions, OAuth scopes or token scopes. API usage has rate limits. Some specific operations impose higher gates, such as Premium or Enterprise for bulk archive.

interfaces.summary: REST API v3 is latest; v2 has the same operation set, while v3 supports ADF in rich-text fields. Official Atlassian CLI (ACLI) has Jira Cloud commands. REST reference includes language examples; no official general-purpose SDK was established in sources checked.

mcp.summary: Atlassian-maintained remote MCP server; recommended endpoint https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp. Supports Jira read, write, search; delete and manage groups require admin enablement. OAuth 2.1 is default; API-token modes require admin enablement. User permissions, scopes, IP allowlists, and domain settings apply. No community server asserted; no community maintainer source was collected.

buildability.summary: Can build against REST v3 using a Free site and OAuth/API token; can reuse vendor MCP or ACLI. Public distribution needs separate OAuth/Marketplace review and security prerequisites; customer-site authorization and relevant scopes/permissions are required.

first.blocker: For private prototype, create a Free Jira site and developer-console 3LO app; use least-privilege scopes and test enhanced JQL search. For public OAuth, implement a single distributable 3LO app, enable sharing, complete partner/security prerequisites, then submit for Atlassian approval. For MCP token mode, ask organization admin to enable it and issue a scoped token/key.

verified.description: Atlassian cloud project and work tracking service. Jira Software and Jira Work Management were unified under the Jira name in 2024.

auth.summary: Jira REST integrations support OAuth 2.0 three-legged authorization; account API tokens use Basic auth. Atlassian MCP also documents API-token modes, including a service-account key sent as Bearer. These credentials have distinct identities and issuance paths.

test_access.summary: A Jira Cloud Free site can serve as a test tenant, with up to 10 users. It is a real Jira site, not a dedicated REST sandbox. Requires an Atlassian account and site.

production_access.summary: Core REST features are available on Free and paid plans, subject to user permissions and credentials. Some operations have higher gates: archive-by-JQL requires Premium or Enterprise. Rate limits apply; administrative operations can require admin roles.

interfaces.summary: Jira Cloud REST v3 is the latest platform API; v2 offers the same operations, while v3 supports ADF in specified rich-text fields. Atlassian CLI (ACLI) provides Jira Cloud commands. Official REST docs include language examples; a general-purpose official SDK was not established in checked sources.

mcp.summary: Atlassian-maintained remote MCP endpoint: https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp. Jira read, write and search tool groups are documented; delete and manage groups require admin enablement. OAuth 2.1 is default; token modes require admin enablement. User permissions, scopes and organization policies constrain access. Community MCP status remains unverified; no maintainer source was checked.

buildability.summary: Private REST, vendor MCP and ACLI routes are currently documented; each needs site access and appropriate credentials/permissions. Public distribution adds OAuth sharing and Marketplace review requirements.

verified.blocker: For a private prototype, create a Free site and 3LO app; test least-privilege JQL search. For public distribution, implement one shareable 3LO app and complete partner/security prerequisites before Marketplace submission. For MCP token mode, obtain organization-admin enablement and the appropriate key.

first.description: Cloud work management platform; API and MCP expose workspace tasks, projects, and related Work Graph data.

auth.summary: PAT is long-lived, user-identity bearer credential. OAuth authorization-code app uses client ID, client secret, access token and refresh token. Service Account token is separate, Enterprise-tier and super-admin-created; organization-wide access. MCP OAuth token is separate and MCP-only.

test_access.summary: Use an existing workspace, free account, or request a temporary developer sandbox; sandbox approval is not guaranteed and may take up to one week.

production_access.summary: API access available to authenticated accounts subject to user permissions and plan-dependent limits. PAT/Service Account stays within member workspaces. Public OAuth distribution requires app review; workspace app management can block integrations.

interfaces.summary: REST v1 JSON/form-encoded API; official JavaScript/Python clients; Asana CLI. Official hosted MCP uses Streamable HTTP.

mcp.summary: Official Asana MCP V2 server supports workspace data read/write through OAuth. User authorization selects a workspace; user permissions remain enforced. Developer-facing server and end-user clients documented; no community MCP maintainer verified. Composio search supplied toolkit leads, not proof of API/server availability.

buildability.summary: Private route: wrap REST API with PAT or private OAuth app; sandbox optional and useful for paid features. MCP route: connect to vendor V2 with pre-registered MCP OAuth app. Public OAuth route requires distribution to any workspace and Asana review; public directory listing also requires approval.

first.blocker: For public route, complete app listing checklist, configure any-workspace distribution, submit for review, resolve QA findings, then publish. For paid-feature testing, submit sandbox request. For organization-wide access, obtain Enterprise domain and super-admin-created Service Account. For MCP, create MCP app, register client redirect, and ensure workspace does not block it.

verified.description: Asana work management SaaS; REST API exposes workspace data.

auth.summary: REST supports user-attributed PATs, user-authorized OAuth, and Enterprise Service Account tokens. MCP app tokens are separate and MCP-only.

test_access.summary: Test with an existing/free account or request a developer sandbox. Sandbox approval is not guaranteed; it can take up to a week, has limited users, supports requested paid features, and lasts at most one year.

production_access.summary: REST works with authorized accounts; standard limits are 150 requests/minute for free domains and 1,500 for paid. Public OAuth distribution requires review; Service Accounts require Enterprise and a super admin. Enterprise+ and Legacy Enterprise admins can block MCP clients.

interfaces.summary: REST API v1; official JavaScript and Python libraries; Asana CLI; hosted MCP V2 uses Streamable HTTP.

mcp.summary: Official Asana MCP V2 is generally available for workspace reads and writes. Developers pre-register an OAuth MCP app; tokens are MCP-only, user permissions apply, and available tools vary. No community integration was independently verified. Supplied Composio matches are research leads only.

buildability.summary: Private REST route uses PAT or private OAuth app; sandbox is optional for paid-feature testing. MCP route requires a pre-registered OAuth app. Public OAuth route requires Any workspace distribution and review. Service Account route requires Enterprise and super-admin provisioning.

verified.blocker: Private: create app, set workspace distribution, configure OAuth or PAT, and test in an account or approved sandbox. Public: set Any workspace, complete listing and security requirements, submit review, resolve findings, then publish. Service Account: obtain Enterprise domain and super-admin provisioning. MCP: register app and redirect URL; ask admin to allow it if blocked.

first.product: monday.com — platform API and Apps Framework. Category: Productivity and Project Management.
first.description: Monday.com work management platform. Platform API operates on boards, items, columns and related workspace objects. API covers monday work management, dev, sales CRM and service; Workforms unsupported. Edition/deployment checked: hosted monday.com platform; account region and deployment-specific API host not established in public docs checked.

auth.summary: Personal V2 API token identifies its user and mirrors UI permissions; send in Authorization header. OAuth app tokens use granted scopes. OAuth 2.1 needs app client_id/client_secret and PKCE verifier. Personal tokens available to API-enabled admins/members; guest can use OAuth or short-lived token, not personal API key. Viewers, deactivated/disabled users, unconfirmed-email users and student accounts cannot access API.

test_access.summary: Free developer account provides an isolated environment for app/API development without production data. Developer accounts include Free-plan features plus higher limits and selected Pro/Enterprise capabilities; documented limits include 10 seats, 1,000 items per product, API complexity limit 10M. Any account can explore the Apps Framework; existing accounts can use API subject to user eligibility.

production_access.summary: Production API calls use an eligible live monday.com user/account and actual UI permissions; no API-wide paid minimum was established in checked docs. Developer Apps can be installed privately or shared publicly. Marketplace distribution requires submission and approval; app monetization plans/pricing are separate from platform API access. Hosted MCP client access has documented account/admin gates by route.

interfaces.summary: Platform API is GraphQL over HTTP POST at https://api.monday.com/v2; JSON request body carries query/mutation. Version via API-Version header. Official JS/TS SDK @mondaydotcomorg/api; setup-api CLI scaffolds codegen. Official MCP uses Streamable HTTP. Public schema route is /v2/get_schema?version=2026-10; authenticated inspection was not available here.

mcp.summary: Vendor Platform MCP: hosted https://mcp.monday.com/mcp, >60 tools to read/write customer workspace data; OAuth or personal token. Vendor Apps MCP: local npm package mode=apps, API token; developer tasks such as app/version/deployment/storage management. Community-maintained integration: mondaycom/mcp GitHub repo and @mondaydotcomorg/monday-api-mcp; Node 20+, npm 5.2+, local stdio, personal token; optional read-only mode. Hosted MCP has user-scoped permissions and API daily-call consumption; SSE deprecated. Composio catalogs Monday (126 tools; managed OAuth listed) and Monday MCP (96 tools; Composio-managed OAuth unavailable; DCR_OAUTH). Catalog match is discovery only.

buildability.summary: Justified routes: wrap GraphQL API; reuse hosted or vendor-source MCP; use free developer account first for test. Production needs eligible live user/account access and operation scopes/UI rights. Marketplace publishing separately needs review approval; customer-specific MCP access may need admin approval.

first.blocker: Obtain a free developer account and eligible API user token for test; retrieve https://api.monday.com/v2/get_schema?version=2026-10 and count query/mutation fields from that immutable response. For live route obtain customer-approved OAuth app/install or eligible user authorization, required scopes and tenant/account context. For marketplace obtain review approval.

test_access.summary: A free developer account provides isolated test data. Documented limits include 10 seats, 1,000 items per product and API complexity limit 10M. Existing eligible accounts can also use the API, subject to user and object permissions.

production_access.summary: Live API calls require an eligible account and user permissions; checked docs establish no universal paid API minimum. Marketplace publication and certain hosted MCP connector routes have separate approval gates.

interfaces.summary: GraphQL over HTTP POST at https://api.monday.com/v2, versioned with API-Version header. Official JS/TS SDK and codegen CLI are published. Vendor MCP uses Streamable HTTP.

mcp.summary: Vendor hosted Platform MCP at https://mcp.monday.com/mcp offers over 60 read/write tools for workspace data. Vendor Apps MCP is local developer tooling. mondaycom/mcp maintains a local npm integration. Composio catalogs Monday and Monday MCP as research leads; catalog coverage and auth are not proof of vendor API/MCP absence or completeness.

buildability.summary: Can wrap GraphQL or reuse hosted/vendor MCP; free developer account supports initial tests. Live access requires an eligible account/user; marketplace release requires review approval.

test_access.summary: No separate API sandbox documented. Test with an existing ClickUp account and personal token; Try It runs against the Workspace associated with that token. Public API is available on all plans.

production_access.summary: Public API available across plans; some routes/parameters are Enterprise-only. OAuth app creation requires Workspace owner/admin. Plan limits are feature gates, not API trial caps.

interfaces.summary: REST API v2 with selected v3 endpoints; official reference publishes raw v2 and v3 OpenAPI links. Official GitHub plugin is a client integration, not API SDK. No ClickUp-maintained SDK or CLI verified.

mcp.summary: Official hosted remote MCP at `https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp`, available all plans, OAuth-only; signed-in user's permissions apply. Community servers exist; maintainers include `trustxai` and `rubenaguir`. Official plugin also packages workflow skills for developer clients.

buildability.summary: Private integration: wrap public API with personal token or reuse hosted MCP after OAuth. Public multi-customer app: OAuth authorization-code app; obtain owner/admin-created app credentials. MCP client can reuse official remote server.

first.blocker: For private prototype, generate a personal token in an existing non-customer Workspace and use low-impact read operations. verified.description: ClickUp project-management SaaS with a public API and a hosted MCP server.

test_access.summary: No separate API sandbox is documented. Testing requires an existing account and token; Try It calls the Workspace associated with the token. No fixture tenant is documented.

production_access.summary: Public API is available on all plans. Individual routes or parameters have plan gates, including Enterprise-only user and guest management. Workspace owners/admins must create OAuth apps.

interfaces.summary: REST API v2 with selected v3 endpoints. Official raw OpenAPI files are linked; no vendor-maintained general-purpose SDK or CLI was verified. The official plugin connects to hosted MCP.

mcp.summary: ClickUp hosts remote MCP at `https://mcp.clickup.com/mcp`; it uses OAuth and the signed-in user's permissions. Community servers are also published by `trustxai` and `rubenaguir`. The ClickUp plugin is a client integration, not a separate MCP service.

buildability.summary: Private integration can wrap the API with a personal token or use hosted MCP with OAuth. Public multi-user API app needs an owner/admin-created OAuth app and its credentials. Routes depend on the user's account and any endpoint-specific plan gates.

verified.blocker: Private prototype: generate a personal token in a non-customer Workspace and begin with read-only operations. Public app: have a Workspace owner/admin create the OAuth app, register the redirect URI, and provide client credentials; restrict features to plan-eligible operations. first.description: Collaborative docs and workflow platform; public REST API for docs, pages, tables, rows, formulas, controls, and more.

test_access.summary: No separate API sandbox documented. API access uses an account token against the live service; free Coda accounts can issue tokens. Coda MCP free access is limited by role and request allowance.

production_access.summary: API rate limits are not plan-dependent, and API tokens are available in account settings. API access is unavailable for docs over 125 MB. MCP full access is included for Doc Makers on paid plans; free-plan Doc Makers and Editors have 30 requests/week, max 60/month.

interfaces.summary: REST API v1 over HTTPS with JSON; official developer reference and OpenAPI 3.0 JSON/YAML are published. Google Apps Script is the only officially supported API client library; Packs SDK is for building Packs. MCP is a separate interface.

mcp.summary: Vendor-hosted MCP at https://coda.io/apis/mcp, beta, for customer docs and data. Official OAuth2 PKCE or MCP-restricted personal token; available tools include read/search and create, update, delete. Free-tier usage and role restrictions apply. Officially supported legacy Coda MCP remains available; vendor says it will be deprecated in the near future.

buildability.summary: Private integrations can wrap the documented REST API with an account token or reuse the hosted MCP. Public distribution can use the documented API, but each end user needs an account token; OAuth for the REST API is not documented. MCP public availability depends on client auth support and token/role limits.

first.blocker: For direct integration, obtain an account token and validate against a non-sensitive test doc. For OAuth MCP, configure a supported client against https://coda.io/apis/mcp; endpoints are client-discovery driven.

verified.description: Collaborative docs and workflow platform. Public REST API v1 supports docs, tables, rows, pages, formulas, and controls.

test_access.summary: No separate API sandbox or test tenant documented. Use an account token against production, preferably a test document. This is an inference from the published API reference and token setup.

production_access.summary: Public REST API is available to all users; API rate limits are plan-independent. Docs over 125 MB may not support API calls. interfaces.summary: REST API v1 over HTTPS with JSON; published reference and OpenAPI 3.0 JSON/YAML links. Google Apps Script is the only supported API client library; Packs SDK is for Pack development. No official API CLI found; MCP client setup is separately documented.

mcp.summary: Vendor-hosted Docs MCP at https://docs.superhuman.com/apis/mcp; customer-data tools include read, search, create, update, and delete operations. The older Coda endpoint https://coda.io/apis/mcp remains supported but is slated for deprecation. MCP has role/request limits; no install-count cap documented.

buildability.summary: Private route: wrap REST with an account token or reuse hosted MCP. Public route: REST requires per-user token setup; hosted MCP OAuth is available to supported clients. REST public OAuth registration is undocumented. Access requires a user account and permissions to target content.

verified.blocker: For private build, issue a least-privilege API token and validate against a test doc. For a public REST app, obtain vendor confirmation of supported OAuth/app registration (none found in reviewed docs) or implement per-user token onboarding. For inventory, retrieve the linked OpenAPI JSON in a network-enabled environment and count operations by tag/family.

first.description: Collaborative work management platform for sheets, projects, reports, dashboards and workflows. General API: Business, Enterprise or Advanced Work Management per introduction; OpenAPI reference banner still says Business and Enterprise. API and SDK use governed by Developer Agreement.

auth.summary: Personal API access token: generate in Personal Settings → API Access; copy once, revoke/manage there. It acts as the issuing user's access, including their data read/write permissions; use `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Regional accounts use separate tokens.
